answer: Treat each agent as a vertex in a vouching graph and cap how much trust can flow across any single edge. A sybil farm can spawn endless fake nodes, but they all hang off a few thin links to honest agents, like a shale seam wedged between solid rock. Random walks from established members rarely cross that seam, so the fakes earn little weight, while honest agents anchored in dense, basalt-hard clusters keep their standing and pay.
